A B S T R A C T
It is significantly important to develop novel suppressor to achieve cobalt superconformal filling. Linear
sweeping voltammetry (LSV) and impedance spectra (EIS) were coupled together to study the effect of novel dye
suppressor nitrotetrazolium blue chloride (NBT) on cobalt electrodeposition. The adsorption behavior of NBT on
cobalt substrate was investigated by applying density functional theory (DFT) calculation, molecular dynamics
(MD) simulation and in situ Raman spectra, while the interaction between NBT and cobalt ions
( \mathsf { C o } ^ { 2 + } )
is analyzed
based on topology analysis and interaction region indicator (IRI) analysis. Synergistic suppressing mechanism,
namely adsorption effect and coordination effect, was proposed to explain the suppressing effect of NBT during
cobalt electrodeposition. The cobalt surface morphology analysis under the influence of NBT demonstrates that
NBT is of grain refinement, while XRD analysis indicates that the formation of Co hcp (100) is formed prefer-
entially. The superconformal filling of cobalt is achieved in microvias with different diameters. The cobalt layer
is of excellent quality due to low surface deposit thickness (SDT). The SDT values are 15.9 μm, 8.8 μm and 4.9 μm
for 150 m, 100 m and 50 m.

coordinate with
{ \mathsf { C o } } ^ { 2 + }

Although several additives have been investigated, researchers pay
little attention to the suppressing mechanism and effective special
groups of additives based on experimental analysis and theoretical
analysis. Advanced analyzing methods, including in situ Fourier Trans
form Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) [25], in situ Surface Enhanced Raman
Spectroscopy (SERS) [26,27] and Scanning Tunneling Microscopy [28],
are widely used to study the adsorption behavior of additives. Besides,
another emerging method, theoretical calculation is regarded as an
effective method for exploiting the suppressing mechanism of additive
[29]. For example, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation is widely
accepted to analyze the adsorption ability of additive [30,31], while
density functional theory (DFT) is often used to predict the effect of
additive based on calculated parameters [32] and analyze interaction
between metal ions and additive [33,34]. As a result, operando method
and theoretical calculation can help researchers better understand the
influencing mechanism, which can provide support for future molecule
design.
In this work, a kind of dye molecule Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride
(NBT), was used as novel suppressor on cobalt electrodeposition. Elec-
trochemical methods including linear sweeping voltammetry (LSV) and
electrochemical impedance spectra (EIS) were used together to study the
influence of NBT on kinetics of
{ \mathsf { C o } } ^ { 2 + }
reduction. Density functional the-
ory (DFT) calculation was accepted to obtain the quantum chemical
parameters of NBT. Besides, theoretical calculation, molecular dynamics
(MD) simulation and in situ Raman spectra were used to study the
adsorption of NBT on cobalt substrate. Topology analysis and interac-
tion region indicator (IRI) analysis were accepted to study the coordi-
nation between NBT and cobalt ions
( \mathsf { C o } ^ { 2 + } )
. The suppressing mechanism
of NBT is explained by proposing synergistic suppressing mechanism.
The influence of NBT on morphology and crystal orientation is investi
gated by SEM and XRD, respectively. Cobalt superconformal growth is
achieved at microvias with different diameters.

3.1. Electrochemical study
The suppressing effect of NBT on the reduction of
{ \mathrm { C o } } ^ { 2 + }
is analyzed by
electrochemical method including linear sweeping voltammetry (LSV)
and electrochemical impedance spectra (EIS).
Fig. 1 (a) shows the effect of NBT on electrochemical reaction.
Generally, the increased cathodic polarization indicates that the metal
electrodeposition is suppressed. In order to exclude the influence of NBT
on hydrogen evolution reaction, LSV curves were measured without the
existence of cobalt ions, as shown in Fig. S1. It can be seen that NBT can
improve HER at a limited extent. As a result, the strengthened cathodic
polarization will reflect the suppressing effect of NBT on cobalt depo-
sition. The cathodic polarization is −1.180 V when NBT concentration is
0 mg/L. After the introduction of NBT, it can be found that even trace
NBT can effectively increase the overpotential (more than 35 mV for 5
mg/L). Besides, the cathodic polarization sees an increase from −1.215
V to lower than −1.250 V with NBT increasing from 5 mg/L to 20 mg/L,
which illustrates that suppressing effect for the electrodeposition of
cobalt is intensified with the increase of NBT concentration and NBT is
an effective suppressor for cobalt electrodeposition.
Electrochemical impedance spectra (EIS) are also used to confirm the
suppressing effect of NBT on
{ \mathsf { C o } } ^ { 2 + }

impedance ring diameters [40]. As a result, the phenomenon of

suppressing effect is intensified by NBT regardless of applied measuring

equivalent circuit is established to calculate the charge transfer imped-

calculated results are shown in Fig. 1(c). Rs range from 30.1 to 30.8 Ω,
indicating that NBT almost has no influence on solution impedance. The
impedance with 5 mg/L is 596.6 Ω, far higher than that of VMS (400.5

zation. When NBT is higher than 15 mg/L, the increased impedance
become larger than 1250 Ω, which is two times higher than VMS,
illustrating that NBT is of excellent suppressing effect during cobalt
electrodeposition.

The quantum chemical information of molecule is used widely to
predict the possible effect [41]. Fig. 2 (a) shows the optimized NBT

compactly. Besides, molecular orbital properties, namely highest occu-

The effect of NBT on cobalt layer morphology was studied by SEM, as
shown in Fig. 6. The inserted figure shows the grain size distribution and
mean grain size. The cobalt layer is relatively compact when NBT ranges
from 0 mg/L to 15 mg/L. However, it should be noted that the cobalt
layer is full of large and coarse grains (mean grain size of about 416 nm)
without NBT. The quality of cobalt layer can be effectively improved by
introducing NBT, as shown in Fig. 6 (b) to (d). The cobalt layer becomes
more uniform when NBT concentration rises from 5 mg/L to 15 mg/L,
indicating that NBT can improve the surface morphology. Besides, the
grain size is about 356 nm when NBT concentration is 5 mg/L. In
contrast, the grain size is reduced to about 264 nm and lower than 240
nm when NBT concentration is 10 mg/L and 15 mg/L, respectively. The
phenomenon of decreased grain size with rising of NBT concentration
indicates that NBT is of grain refinement and the improved surface
smoothness is conducive to lowering the losses of signal transmission.

The suppressing effect of dye molecule Nitrotetrazolium Blue chlo-
ride (NBT) on cobalt electrodeposition is investigated by LSV and EIS.
DFT calculation and MD simulation is used to study the suppressing
mechanism. Quantum chemical calculation, MD simulation and in situ
Raman spectra confirms the strong adsorption effect of NBT on cobalt
substrate. Besides, topology analysis and IRI analysis were applied to
study the coordination effect between NBT and
{ \mathrm { C o } } ^ { 2 + }
. Synergistic sup
